$$
\begin{aligned}u={e}^{4x}\, & ⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=4{e}^{4x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\, & ⇒\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int {e}^{4x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{4x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\int (\operatorname{sin}⁡x)(4{e}^{4x})\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{4x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-4\int {e}^{4x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{4x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-4J.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we can use integration by parts to evaluate

$$
J=\int {e}^{4x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x.
$$

To do this, let's suppose that

$$
\begin{aligned}u={e}^{4x}\, & ⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=4{e}^{4x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\, & ⇒\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}J & =\int {e}^{4x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{4x}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)(4{e}^{4x})\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{4x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x+4\int {e}^{4x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{4x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x+4I.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this back into our equation for $I,$ we can subsequently solve for $I.$ We remember to add a constant of integration $C$ at the end.

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={e}^{4x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-4J \\ I & ={e}^{4x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-4(-{e}^{4x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x+4I) \\ I & ={e}^{4x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+4{e}^{4x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-16I \\ 17I & ={e}^{4x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+4{e}^{4x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ I & =\frac{{e}^{4x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+4\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}{17}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's denote the indefinite integral by $I=\int {e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x.$

To use integration by parts, let's suppose that

$$
\begin{aligned}u={e}^{x}\, & ⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}={e}^{x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\, & ⇒\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int {e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\int (\operatorname{sin}⁡x)({e}^{x})\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\int {e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-J.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we can use integration by parts to evaluate

$$
J=\int {e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x.
$$

To do this, let's suppose that

$$
\begin{aligned}u={e}^{x}\, & ⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}={e}^{x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\, & ⇒\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}J & =\int {e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{x}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)({e}^{x})\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\int {e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x+I.\end{aligned}
$$

So, substituting this into our equation for $I,$ we can subsequently solve for $I:$

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-J \\ I & ={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-(-{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x+I) \\ I & ={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-I \\ 2I & ={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ I & =\frac{{e}^{x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate our definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =(\frac{{e}^{x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}{2}){|}_{-\pi }^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{{e}^{\pi }(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi ))}{2}-\frac{{e}^{-\pi }(\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\pi )+\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\pi ))}{2} \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{\pi }}{2}+\frac{{e}^{-\pi }}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({e}^{-\pi }-{e}^{\pi })\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the indefinite integral by  $I=\int {e}^{-4x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x.$

To use integration by parts, let's suppose that 

$$
\begin{aligned}u={e}^{-4x}\, & ⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-4{e}^{-4x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\, & ⇒\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int {e}^{-4x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =({e}^{-4x})(-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)(-4{e}^{-4x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-4x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-4\int {e}^{-4x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-4x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-4J.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we can use integration by parts to evaluate

$$
J=\int {e}^{-4x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x.
$$

To do this, let's suppose that

$$
\begin{aligned}u={e}^{-4x}\, & ⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-4{e}^{-4x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\, & ⇒\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}J & =\int {e}^{-4x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =({e}^{-4x})(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-\int (\operatorname{sin}⁡x)(-4{e}^{-4x})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{-4x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+4I.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into our equation for $I,$ we solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =-{e}^{-4x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-4({e}^{-4x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+4I) \\ I & =-{e}^{-4x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-4{e}^{-4x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-16I \\ 17I & =-{e}^{-4x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x+4\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\ I & =-\frac{{e}^{-4x}}{17}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x+4\operatorname{sin}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate our definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{e}^{-4x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =(-\frac{{e}^{-4x}}{17}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x+4\operatorname{sin}⁡x)){|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =(-\frac{{e}^{-4\pi }}{17}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )+4\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )))-(-\frac{1}{17}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)+4\operatorname{sin}⁡(0))) \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{-4\pi }}{17}(-1+0)+\frac{1}{17}(1+0) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{-4\pi }}{17}+\frac{1}{17} \\  & =\frac{1}{17}(1+{e}^{-4\pi }).\end{aligned}
$$
